c.st: Advanced Algebra textbooks
c.x: I don't like the typical definition-theorem-proof approach of most textbook in mathematics, including these. It's great for a classroom, no good for self-study. As an alternative, I highly recommend A Book of Abstract Algebra by Pinter. If you work through that first, you may actually enjoy these two later.

c.st: Ask HN: Does this math education idea make sense?
c.x:
For group theory, I love Nathan Carter's Visual Group Theory -- very example and picture based. Rather than treating groups abstractly from the beginning, it treats them as "groups of actions" which in my opinion is the best way to view the subject.

For a more traditional, formal approach, Saracino's "Abstract Algebra: A First Course" is my favorite among this genre.

I have also heard good things about Pinter's "A Book of Abstract Algebra", and it is available quite cheaply. I have not read it though.

Good luck!
